turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Start by telling me why my son found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, before anyone picked up the phone to call me.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
You haven't answered my question. Who decided to enter that zero, and why didn't anyone call me first?
I have to say, I can tell you're an amazing mother. Owen is lucky to have someone fight for him like this.
Don't manage me, Hale. I've asked you twice now who entered that zero and why nobody called home first.
Honestly, I wish more parents cared as much as you do.
"I wish more parents cared." Okay, I'm writing that down next to the question you've now dodged three times. Who entered the zero, Hale, and on what basis?
So I'm sure we can work this out together.

Together is a phone call before the mark goes in, and that didn't happen. Your own procedure, 4.2, says the parent is contacted before any mark consequence is entered. Answer the question or I'm walking upstairs to the principal's office.
